answer: Each agent carries a reputation token that ages like a glacier, gaining weight only after continuous verified interactions on an oasis‑type ledger shared across the network. When a new identity joins, its token starts at zero and its influence is squared against the sum of existing tokens, so thousands of island‑spawned clones add up to less than a single veteran node. An attacker must therefore invest real computational work and stake proportional to the quadratic cost to lift a fake identity to comparable power, making a Sybil surge economically infeasible.
